questions.question: Which team topped the medal tally at the 2025 National Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Services Sports Control Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB)** is a major contributor to India's sporting achievements, particularly in national events like the National Games.
 
• The **SSCB** has consistently topped the medal tally in various editions of the National Games due to its strong representation in sports like athletics, boxing, wrestling, and shooting.
 
• The organization primarily consists of athletes from the armed forces, including the Army, Navy, and Air Force, who receive extensive training and support. *Hence, the statement about SSCB is correct.*
 
• **Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh** are also key participants in the National Games but typically do not surpass SSCB in overall medal tallies.
 
• Maharashtra and Karnataka often rank high due to their focus on sports development and infrastructure but still fall short of SSCB’s consistent dominance. *Hence, the statements about Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh are incorrect.*
 
• The National Games are conducted to promote sports and identify talent across various states, but SSCB’s athletes often dominate the medal tally due to their rigorous training and discipline.
 
• This consistent performance is also a reflection of the armed forces’ emphasis on physical fitness and sports excellence. *Hence, SSCB is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB):**

 
 
• **SSCB** represents athletes from the Indian armed forces and focuses on developing talent in various sports disciplines.
 
• The organization has a structured approach to training and prepares athletes for national and international competitions.
 
• SSCB athletes are known for their discipline, fitness, and performance, which are key factors in their dominance at the National Games.
 
 
 
• **Other States in National Games:**
 
 
• **Karnataka:** Known for sports like swimming, hockey, and athletics, Karnataka often ranks high but does not surpass SSCB.
 
• **Maharashtra:** A strong contender in disciplines like gymnastics, kabaddi, and shooting, Maharashtra is always among the top-performing states.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:** Focuses on sports development in archery and athletics but has not topped the National Games medal tally.
 
 
 
• **National Games Overview:**
 
 
• The National Games are the premier multi-sport event in India, held periodically to encourage sportsmanship and identify national talent.
 
• It includes competitions in various sports disciplines, with participation from states and organizations like SSCB.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SSCB’s Dominance:**

 
 
• The disciplined training and dedication of armed forces personnel contribute to SSCB’s consistent success in the National Games.
 
• SSCB’s performance often sets a benchmark for other states and organizations participating in the event.
 
 
 
• **National Games History:**
 
 
• The first National Games were held in 1924, and since then, it has been a platform for showcasing India's sporting talent.
 
• The Games include sports disciplines ranging from athletics to indigenous sports like kabaddi.

questions.question: The Employees’ Enrolment Scheme – 2025, launched to promote voluntary EPF compliance and extend social security coverage, was introduced under which Union Ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Labour & Employment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, launched the Employees’ Enrolment Scheme – 2025 at EPFO’s 73rd Foundation Day in New Delhi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Launched by:** Ministry of Labour & Employment under Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.
 
• **Scheme Duration:** Open from 1 November 2025 to 30 April 2026.
 
• **Coverage:** For employees left out of EPF coverage between 1 July 2017 and 31 October 2025.
 
• **Objective:** Promote voluntary compliance and ensure universal EPF inclusion to strengthen “Social Security for All.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)**__

 __
 
• Established: 1952 under the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.
 
• Function: Provides retirement benefits and social security to India’s organized workforce.
 
• Administrative Authority: Ministry of Labour & Employment.
 
 
 
• **Scheme Features**__
 __
 
• Waiver of employee’s share for non-deducted periods.
 
• Employer’s liability limited to employer’s share, interest, admin charges, and ₹100 penal damages.
 
• Applicable to all establishments regardless of existing EPF coverage.
 
 
 
• **Relevant Legal Provisions**__
 
 
• Section 7A – Determination of money due from employers.
 
• Para 26B – Membership of Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS-1995).
 
• Para 8 – Administrative provisions for EPS-1995.

questions.question: Who among the following was posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in January 2025 for his or contribution to literature and education?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MT Vasudevan Nair**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MT Vasudevan Nair**, one of the most celebrated authors in Indian literature, was posthumously awarded the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan** in January 2025 for his outstanding contributions to **literature and education.**
 
• He is a renowned writer, screenwriter, and filmmaker from **Kerala**. His works largely reflect the socio-cultural ethos of Kerala and its people.
 
• Sharda Sinha also won Padma Vibhushan(Posthumously) in January 2025 but in the field of Art, while Osamu Suzuki won Padma Vibhushan(Posthumously) in January 2025 in the field of trade and industry.
 
• **MT Vasudevan Nair** is widely regarded as one of the finest writers in Malayalam literature, having authored several novels, short stories, and scripts for films. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India, and its posthumous conferment on him highlights his immense impact on Indian literature and culture.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is MT Vasudevan Nair.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MT Vasudevan Nair:**

 
 
• **MT Vasudevan Nair**, born on **July 15, 1933**, is a prominent Malayalam writer, widely celebrated for his literary brilliance.
 
• His novel **Randamoozham**, a retelling of the Mahabharata from Bhima's perspective, is regarded as a literary masterpiece.
 
• He has also contributed significantly to **Indian cinema**, writing screenplays for critically acclaimed films such as "Oru Vadakkan Veeragatha" and "Kadavu."
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan:**
 
 
• The **Padma Vibhushan** is India's second-highest civilian award, established in **1954**, and is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service.
 
• It is conferred on individuals from various fields such as art, literature, education, sports, medicine, and public affairs.
 
• Posthumous awards are rare but are given to honor individuals whose contributions are extraordinary and impactful.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Osamu Suzuki**: A Japanese businessman, known for his leadership in the Suzuki Motor Corporation, but has no connection to Indian literature or education.
 
• **Kumudini Lakhia**: An Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer known for her contributions to Indian classical dance, not literature or education.
 
• **Sharda Sinha**: An Indian folk singer known for her songs in Bhojpuri and Maithili, but not associated with the Padma Vibhushan in 2025.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Details About Padma Vibhushan:**

 
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is awarded by the **Government of India** under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• It is announced annually on **Republic Day** (January 26).
 
 
 
• **Notable Recipients:**
 
 
• **APJ Abdul Kalam:** Former President of India and scientist.
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar:** Legendary playback singer.
 
• **Birju Maharaj:** Renowned Kathak dancer.

questions.question: What is India's rank in the New Climate Risk Index Report, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ninth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's rank in the New Climate Risk Index Report, 2025** is Ninth, as per the latest analysis of global vulnerability to climate change and weather extremes.
 
• The **Climate Risk Index (CRI)** is an annual report published by the **Germanwatch organization**, which evaluates and ranks countries based on the impact of extreme weather events such as storms, floods, and heatwaves.
 
• India's high ranking in the CRI reflects its significant vulnerability to climate change-related disasters such as cyclones, floods, and droughts. *Hence, India's rank is ninth.*
 
• The CRI takes into consideration factors such as the **number of fatalities, monetary losses, and human development impacts** to assess the vulnerability of countries. India has witnessed severe climate events in recent years, contributing to its position in the index.
 
• India’s geographical location, with its long coastline and diverse climatic zones, makes it particularly prone to extreme weather conditions, which significantly impact its economy and population. *Hence, the ranking is justified.*
 
• India's rank also highlights the need for **strong climate resilience policies** and global cooperation to address the challenges posed by climate change.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is ninth.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Climate Risk Index (CRI):**

 
 
• The **Climate Risk Index** is an analysis conducted by **Germanwatch** to assess the impact of weather-related loss events globally. It analyzes data from the **NatCatSERVICE database** of Munich Re.
 
• The CRI considers **four indicators**: number of deaths, number of deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, absolute losses in US dollars, and losses per unit of GDP, to rank countries based on their vulnerability.
 
 
 
• **India’s Vulnerability to Climate Change:**
 
 
• India faces extreme weather events such as **cyclones (e.g., Cyclone Amphan in 2020), floods (e.g., Kerala floods in 2018), droughts, and heatwaves**, which lead to loss of lives, property, and infrastructure.
 
• India is highly dependent on its **agriculture sector**, which is sensitive to climate variations. Erratic monsoons and water scarcity affect crop production and food security.
 
• **Coastal regions**, such as West Bengal, Odisha, and Gujarat, face threats from rising sea levels and storm surges, impacting millions of people and causing economic losses.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken by India:**
 
 
• India has committed to climate action through the **Paris Agreement** and has set ambitious targets, such as achieving **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**.
 
• Initiatives such as the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** and state-level action plans aim to promote renewable energy, energy efficiency, and water conservation.
 
• India is also investing in **disaster preparedness** and early warning systems to reduce the impact of extreme weather events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Observations of CRI 2025:**

 
 
• The **top-ranking countries** in the CRI 2025 report are those most affected by extreme weather events, such as **Honduras, Myanmar, and Haiti**, in previous years.
 
• Countries with low adaptive capacities, high population density, and dependence on agriculture and fisheries are more vulnerable to climate risks.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• **Developing countries** are disproportionately affected by climate change due to limited resources for adaptation and recovery.
 
• **International efforts**, such as the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**, aim to assist vulnerable nations in addressing climate change through funding and technology transfer.
 
• The **Global Climate Risk Index** serves as a critical tool for policymakers to identify vulnerable regions and prioritize climate action.

questions.question: Which of the following institutes along with ISRO has launched IRIS, a semi-conductor chip?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Technology, Madras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **IRIS (Indian Research and Innovation Semiconductor chip):** The **IRIS chip** is a groundbreaking semiconductor chip developed collaboratively by **ISRO** and **Indian Institute of Technology, Madras**. It marks a significant milestone in India's semiconductor technology advancements.
 
• **Development Collaboration:** The **Indian Institute of Technology, Madras** has played a pivotal role in this collaborative effort with ISRO to launch the IRIS chip. This partnership highlights the institute’s expertise in research and innovation in semiconductor technology. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Purpose:** The IRIS chip is designed to enhance India's capability in **space technology** and strengthen its position in the global semiconductor market. It is expected to be used in various applications, including **satellite systems and defense technology.**
 
• **Significance:** The development of the IRIS chip aligns with India’s ambition to achieve **self-reliance** in semiconductor manufacturing, a critical area for technological and economic growth.
 
• This innovation represents a **major step** toward reducing dependency on imported semiconductors and fostering indigenous technological capabilities. *Hence, the collaboration with IIT Madras is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Institute of Technology, Madras:**

 
 
• **Location:** Situated in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, IIT Madras is among the premier engineering institutions in India.
 
• **Research Excellence:** The institute is renowned for its contributions to **research, technological innovation, and scientific advancements.** It has a strong focus on developing cutting-edge technologies, including semiconductor chips, artificial intelligence, and energy systems.
 
• **Collaborations:** IIT Madras frequently collaborates with leading organizations like ISRO to work on projects of **national importance**, including space technology development.
 
 
 
• **Semiconductor Technology in India:**
 
 
• India has been focusing on strengthening its semiconductor manufacturing capabilities to meet the growing demand for chips in industries like **electronics, defense, and space.**
 
• The government launched initiatives like the **Semiconductor Mission** to promote indigenous production and reduce dependency on foreign imports.
 
• **Example:** The IRIS chip developed by ISRO and IIT Madras is an example of India's efforts to bolster its semiconductor industry.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Role:**
 
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** is India's premier space agency, responsible for developing technologies for space exploration and satellite systems.
 
• ISRO has been instrumental in fostering partnerships with educational institutions like IIT Madras to advance research in critical areas like **semiconductors and space technology.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Semiconductor Scenario:**

 
 
• **Importance:** Semiconductors are critical for various technologies, including **computers, smartphones, defense systems, and space equipment.**
 
• **Challenges:** The global semiconductor market faces issues like **supply chain disruptions** and geopolitical tensions, making indigenous production vital for countries like India.
 
 
 
• **India’s Semiconductor Mission:**
 
 
• **Objective:** Launched by the government to promote **domestic semiconductor manufacturing** and enhance research capabilities.
 
• **Support:** The mission provides **financial incentives and infrastructure** to attract investments and foster innovation in semiconductor technology.

questions.question: Which Indian film won the Best Film Award at the Asian Film Awards 2025?

• The **2025 Asian Film Awards** celebrated films that showcased exceptional storytelling, direction, and performances.
 
• The film **All We Imagine As Light** won the **Best Film Award** at the 2025 Asian Film Awards. This recognition marked a significant achievement for Indian cinema.
 
• **All We Imagine As Light** is a critically acclaimed Indian film that delves into complex human emotions, relationships, and societal issues.
 
• The film stood out among other nominees like **The Disciple**, **The White Tiger**, and **Gully Boy**, which are also notable works of Indian cinema, but they did not win the award in 2025.
 
• The award reflects the growing global recognition of **Indian filmmakers** and their ability to present stories that resonate universally.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is All We Imagine As Light.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Asian Film Awards:**

 
 
• The **Asian Film Awards** were established in **2007** to honor outstanding achievements in Asian cinema. The awards are presented annually by the **Asian Film Awards Academy**.
 
• The awards cover diverse categories such as **Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Actress, and technical awards**, recognizing the entire spectrum of filmmaking.
 
 
 
• **Details about All We Imagine As Light:**
 
 
• **All We Imagine As Light** is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of **identity, human connections, and resilience**.
 
• The film received critical acclaim for its **compelling narrative, stunning cinematography, and powerful performances**.

• **The White Tiger:** A film adaptation of **Aravind Adiga's novel**, highlighting themes of social inequality in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which country has recently formally joined the Abraham Accords, a series of normalisation agreements between Israel and Arab nations brokered by the United States? (Nov 2025)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kazakhstan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The US President confirmed that Kazakhstan has formally joined the Abraham Accords, expanding the circle of Middle Eastern and Central Asian nations normalising relations with Israel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The Abraham Accords are a set of normalisation agreements signed in 2020 between Israel and several Arab countries, mediated by the United States.
 
• They marked a significant shift in Middle East diplomacy by establishing relations with Israel without prior resolution of the Israel–Palestine conflict.
 
• The accords initially included Israel, UAE, Bahrain, Sudan, and Morocco; Kazakhstan has now become the latest nation to join.
 
• The agreements promote economic, technological, and security partnerships while strengthening U.S. strategic influence in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Abraham Accords**__

 __
 
• Brokered by the U.S. administration under President Donald Trump in 2020.
 
• Aimed at normalising diplomatic, economic, and cultural relations between Israel and Arab states.
 
• Named after Abraham, a patriarchal figure common to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
 
 
 
• **Member Countries (as of 2025)**__
 __
 
• Israel
 
• United Arab Emirates (UAE)
 
• Bahrain
 
• Sudan
 
• Morocco
 
• Kazakhstan (new entrant)
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Accords**__
 __
 
• Reduced Israel’s regional isolation and improved Arab–Israeli cooperation.
 
• Boosted trade, investment, and technological collaboration in defence, energy, and innovation sectors.
 
• Created a new model for peace without preconditions related to the Palestinian issue.
 
 
 
• **UAE’s Role**__
 __
 
• First Gulf country to normalise relations with Israel under the Abraham Accords in 2020.
 
• Set the precedent for other nations to follow, encouraging greater diplomatic engagement with Israel.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance for the U.S.**__

questions.question: In which state of India has the World Health Organisation (WHO) opened its first Global Centre for traditional medicines ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Health Organisation (WHO) inaugurated its first Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (GCTM) in Jamnagar, Gujarat, India.
 
• The GCTM was launched on **April 19, 2022**, in collaboration with the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India.
 
• This centre aims to promote the integration of traditional medicines into global health systems and boost research, innovation, and capacity-building in this sector.
 
• Jamnagar was chosen as it is historically significant for Ayurveda and traditional medicine practices, housing the renowned Gujarat Ayurved University.
 
• The launch of GCTM is a testament to India’s leadership in traditional medicine, with the Ayush sector growing significantly over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The World Health Organisation (WHO) is the UN's specialised health agency, founded in **1948**, providing global health leadership by setting standards, monitoring trends, and coordinating responses to health crises like epidemics (e.g., COVID-19, Ebola) and chronic diseases (e.g., cancer, heart disease).
 
• Key functions include promoting universal health coverage, improving access to medicines, strengthening health systems through technical support, and addressing social/environmental health determinants, aiming for better health and well-being for all.
